spans.claim: Robert Hannaford died suddenly in an Underground Railway train
spans.anchor: died suddenly in an Underground Railway train
spans.span: Whereas Robert Hannaford, formerly Superintendent of Police at Sellithwaite, Yorkshire, died suddenly in an Underground Railway train, near Charing Cross (Embankment) Station about 1.

spans.claim: Hannaford was poisoned by some drug administered hours before death
spans.anchor: he was poisoned by some drug or other

spans.claim: The man with stained fingers was James Granett, also poisoned
spans.anchor: the man who had been to see him. Appleyard identified the dead man

spans.claim: Hannaford cut out a portrait of a woman from a newspaper
spans.anchor: cut a photograph out of some illustrated paper
spans.span: When we were coming to town the other day I saw him cut a photograph out of some illustrated paper he was reading in the train, and put it away in his pocket-book--in a pocket-book, I ought to say, for he had two or three pocket-books.

spans.claim: The portrait was of Madame Anita Listorelle, twin sister of Lady Riversreade
spans.anchor: Madame Anita Listorelle
spans.span: He started again as he read it--_Madame Anita Listorelle_.

spans.claim: Lady Riversreade and Madame Listorelle are twin sisters
spans.anchor: Lady Riversreade and Madame Listorelle are, I repeat, twin sisters
spans.span: Lady Riversreade and Madame Listorelle are, I repeat, twin sisters.

spans.claim: Baseverie visited Lady Riversreade twice and was unwelcome
spans.anchor: Lady Riversreade has lately been visited--twice--by a man who called himself Dr. Cyprian Baseverie
spans.span: 'Miss Featherstone,' Rhona went on--'I believe you're aware that Lady Riversreade has lately been visited--twice--by a man who called himself Dr. Cyprian Baseverie?

spans.claim: Baseverie is not a registered medical man and convicted of fraud
spans.anchor: Convicted of fraud at Central Criminal Court, 1917, and struck off Register

spans.claim: Ambrose is a medical man struck off the register for unprofessional conduct
spans.anchor: Struck off Register by General Medical Council for unprofessional conduct, 1918

spans.claim: Ambrose met Hannaford at Victoria Station on the night of the murder
spans.anchor: Ambrose was the man that met Hannaford at Victoria
spans.span: Ambrose was the man that met Hannaford at Victoria, the tall, muffled-up man that Ledbitter saw!

spans.claim: Ambrose was found dead in a laboratory, poisoned
spans.anchor: he and Hetherwick looked in. It had been fitted up as a bed-sitting-room

spans.claim: Baseverie was arrested at Waterloo with the jewels and money
spans.anchor: dramatic arrest of Baseverie at Waterloo
spans.span: Winding up, of course, with the dramatic arrest of Baseverie at Waterloo!

spans.claim: The sealed packet containing the ink formula was stolen and sold by Baseverie
spans.anchor: formula for the ink
spans.span: That's the formula for the ink!

spans.claim: The formula was sold to Culthwaite and Houseover for ten thousand pounds
spans.anchor: we gave this man Baring or Baseverie ten thousand pounds for it
spans.span: We gave this man Baring or Baseverie ten thousand pounds for it, but----" "But you really believe it to be worth more, eh?

spans.claim: The poison was administered in a tonic bottle supplied by chemist Macpherson
spans.anchor: I made up the tonic that was in that bottle
spans.span: And I'll shorten matters by telling you, at once--I made up the tonic that was in that bottle!

spans.claim: The kidnapping of Madame Listorelle and Rhona Hannaford occurred at Riversreade Court
spans.anchor: they were carried off as they crossed from the Court to the Home
spans.span: Lady Riversreade says they were carried off as they crossed from the Court to the Home--she's heard something of a big car with strange men in it.

spans.claim: The kidnappers used a light-colored car with a driver in green livery
spans.anchor: light-coloured car with two men in it, driven by a man who wore a dark-green livery
spans.span: A light-coloured car with two men in it, driven by a man who wore a dark-green livery with gold lace on it!

spans.claim: The two women were held captive in a locked room with barred windows
spans.anchor: fitted with a new patent lock, key outside... window morticed inside and fitted with iron bars outside

spans.claim: The false assumption that Lady Riversreade was Mrs. Whittingham is refuted
spans.anchor: Lady Riversreade is not the woman who was known as Mrs. Whittingham
spans.span: Lady Riversreade is not the woman who was known as Mrs. Whittingham at Sellithwaite ten years ago, nor did Hannaford believe that she was either!

spans.claim: The false solution accusing Lady Riversreade is refuted in chapter 16
spans.anchor: Lady Riversreade is not Mrs. Whittingham. Hannaford did not think she was Mrs. Whittingham
spans.span: Lady Riversreade is not Mrs. Whittingham. Hannaford did not think she was Mrs. Whittingham.
